ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, \(AD\) is the angle bisector of \( \triangle ABC\), \(CE\) is the height of \( \triangle ABC\), \(\angle BAC=50^\circ\), \(\angle BCE=25^\circ\), what is the degree measure of \( \angle ADB\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, and $\angle BAC=50^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BAD=25^\circ$,\\
also given that $CE$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$, and $\angle BCE=25^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BEC=90^\circ$,\\
thus we get $\angle B=65^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle ADB=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle BAD=180^\circ-65^\circ-25^\circ=\boxed{90^\circ}$.
